import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_30/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_30/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# According to operation history:
# 1) JOIN Source2_30_0 and Source2_30_1 on 'city' was done, but final target only needs ['city', 'fare'] with avg fare per city from Source2_30_1
# 2) Then group by Source2_30_1.city and avg(Source2_30_1.fare) was done, which matches the target schema and examples better.

# So final output is average fare per city from Source2_30_1.

# Group by city and average fare
target_df = source1.groupby('city', as_index=False)['fare'].mean()

# Ensure column types match target schema: city (string), fare (float)
target_df['city'] = target_df['city'].astype(str)
target_df['fare'] = target_df['fare'].astype(float)

# Write to target path
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_30/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_30/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_30/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city (inner join to keep only matching cities)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, how='inner', left_on='city', right_on='city')

# Group by city and aggregate average fare
result = joined.groupby('city', as_index=False).agg({'fare': 'mean'})

# Write output with exact target schema and column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_30/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
